question: The Commission has introduced a provisional safeguard measure on imports of grain-oriented electrical steel (GOES), which also covers the cores in imported transformers. The measure supports GOES manufacturers in the EU, including those in Poland.

According to T&D Europe, the association of European manufacturers of transformers and grid technology, the duty of EUR 1 140 per tonne on cores covers only around one third of the price difference, approximately 100 countries are exempt from the measure, and GOES production in the EU stands at around 300 000 tonnes, compared with a demand of around 560 000 tonnes.
The association points out that, as a result, importing finished transformers is becoming economically viable. In light of the above: 1.
If definitive measures are introduced, will the Commission raise the duty on cores in imported transformers to the level of the actual price difference and limit exemptions from the measure?

Apart from the estimate on which it based the duty on cores, has the Commission collected data from transformer manufacturers in the EU and assessed the measure’s impact on the costs of expanding electricity networks, including in Poland?
Will the Commission make the continuation of the measure conditional on binding investment commitments from GOES manufacturers in the EU, so that production within the Union meets demand?
